BREAKING: The average cost of a family’s annual health insurance premium in the US is up +$1,303 YoY, or +5%, to a record $28,303.

This marks the 4th consecutive annual increase of at least +$1,300.

Over this period, the average annual premium for family coverage has surged +$5,884, or +26%.

To put this into perspective, CPI inflation has risen +13% over the same period, or half as much.

Since 1999, the average health insurance premium for a family has soared +$22,494, or +387%.

This represents an average annual growth rate of +6.1%, well above CPI inflation at +2.6% over the same period.

Health insurance has never been more expensive.

1.1 million ethereum:0xad29f2723fcdbcf665f210f25e06f97477e417cf just got permanently removed from circulation.

@grvt_io Not only promised. Not sitting in some treasury waiting for the right moment.

Actually bought on the open market and burned.

That's nearly 1% of the circulating supply at the time, and it's the first completed buyback from GRVT.

The part I like is that you don't have to take their word for it.

There's a public dashboard showing the purchases, burn transactions, and how much supply has been removed.

Future buybacks are intended to happen monthly, although the timing and size remain discretionary.

But here's where things get more interesting.

This is just the first step toward Grvt 2.0.

The roadmap includes:

> Grvt Earn with tokenized fixed-income strategies targeting up to 11% yield, not guaranteed

> Stable Funding Perps covering stocks, FX, commodities, and indices with zero trading fees

> Yield as Margin, allowing eligible Earn balances to support trading positions while continuing to earn yield

> A redesigned self-custodial app bringing everything together

Personally, Yield as Margin is what caught my attention.

Having capital earn yield while also supporting your trading positions is a much more interesting use of funds than leaving margin sitting idle.

Grvt is trying to move beyond being just another place to trade perps.

One balance. Trading and earning connected. Better capital efficiency.

The buyback got my attention.

Now I want to see how much of that Grvt 2.0 vision actually translates into a better trading experience.

Crypto traders have access to many markets, but what if they could trade more than just crypto on one platform?

That’s part of what @grvt_io is working on with Stable Funding Perps.

The product is planned for November 2026 and aims to bring more markets to Grvt, including stocks, forex, commodities, and indices.

Grvt also plans to offer zero trading fees and funding payments that happen once a day.

The goal is to have more than 1,000 markets available by December 2026.

One thing that caught my attention is the daily funding model.

In perpetual trading, funding payments can affect how much it costs to hold a position.

Having these payments happen once a day could make it easier for traders to understand and plan around their positions.

Of course, traders still need to understand how the product works, the risks involved, and the rules for managing their positions.

Also, zero trading fees do not mean there are no other costs or risks to consider.

What I find interesting is the bigger plan.

Grvt wants to go beyond crypto trading and give users access to more markets through one platform.

If everything goes as planned, Stable Funding Perps could become an important part of the Grvt 2.0 expansion.

I’m looking forward to seeing how these markets launch and how easy they will be for users to access and understand.
